page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a cloud-native compute instance configured with 64 shared vCPUs and 384 GB of memory. Powered by AMD EPYC 7542 processors operating at a base clock of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provides one thread per core across 64 physical cores under the KVM hypervisor. Hardware features include L1 data cache of 64 KB, 0.5 MB L2 cache per core, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, along with standard instruction sets including AVX, AES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, integrated GPUs, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote block storage and external networking configurations for production deployment. Its memory profile provides 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it between standard general-purpose and dedicated memory-optimized profiles. In memory subsystem testing, the platform achieves 3,728.41 GB/sec on cached read benchmarks, while uncached 256 MB reads and writes register at 132.51 GB/sec and 90.89 GB/sec respectively.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear bifurcation between single-threaded and parallel performance. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng (744.89) and Geekbench single-core (1155.0), fall into lower performance percentiles due to conservative 2.0 GHz clock frequencies and shared core scheduling. In contrast, parallel tests register strong multi-core scalability, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 60,061.44, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 400.83 GB/sec, and 61.42 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the shared CPU model combined with a high core count offers cost-effective parallel compute density without the overhead of dedicated single-tenant silicon. Tradeoffs center on lower per-thread execution speed and the absence of attached NVMe storage. UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is best suited for horizontally parallel batch processing, distributed compilation, ETL pipelines, in-memory caching layers, and multi-threaded data transformations.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is an x86_64 cloud server featuring 64 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz and 384 GB of system RAM. Governed by a KVM hypervisor, each vCPU maps to a physical core with single-thread allocation. The server includes no bundled local storage, no GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached volumes for data persistence. Benchmark analysis indicates modest single-core throughput alongside strong parallel scaling, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 60,061.44 and multi-threaded bzip3 throughput of 400.83 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains steady at 132.51 GB/sec for uncached block reads. With 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance provides a resource-dense profile well aligned with large-scale batch computation, multi-threaded ETL jobs, distributed builds, and in-memory analytics clusters.
